report.scene_summary: The video shows a warehouse environment with multiple pedestrians walking through aisles and open areas. The scene contains various obstructions including stacked pallets, large wooden crates, and cardboard boxes. Yellow painted lines mark pedestrian walkways and vehicle zones. There are no forklifts or other motorized vehicles visible in the sampled frames, but the layout is designed for mixed pedestrian and vehicle traffic. Pedestrians are seen walking in various directions, some crossing marked lines and moving behind obstructions.

findings.title: Pedestrian blind spot at aisle intersection near pallet stacks
findings.location: left side of warehouse near stacked pallets and work tables
findings.observation: Pedestrians are observed walking behind and around large stacks of wooden pallets (visible in E002, E003, E004, E014, E015). The pallet stacks create a blind corner where a pedestrian could emerge suddenly from behind the stack or where a vehicle approaching the intersection would not see a pedestrian until they are already in the path. In E002, a pedestrian walks from behind the pallet stack area. In E003 and E004, pedestrians are visible near the pallet stacks. The yellow painted line on the floor suggests a designated path, but the physical obstruction of the pallets blocks visibility.
findings.risk_interpretation: A pedestrian could step out from behind the pallet stack into the path of a vehicle without either party seeing the other until it is too late to avoid a collision. This is a classic blind corner scenario.
findings.applicability_reason: The pallet stacks obstruct vision at an intersection where pedestrians and potential vehicles may cross paths.
unknowns: Site-specific traffic rules for this intersection
recommended_actions: Install a convex mirror at the corner of the pallet stack to provide visibility around the blind corner
Mark a stop line with a horn signal requirement before entering the intersection
Consider relocating the pallet stack to improve sight lines
Implement a designated pedestrian crossing point with enhanced visibility

findings.title: Pedestrian blind spot near large wooden crate and box stacks
findings.location: right side of warehouse near large wooden crate and stacked cardboard boxes
findings.observation: Multiple pedestrians are observed walking near and behind large wooden crates and stacks of cardboard boxes (visible in E001, E005, E006, E007, E008, E009, E010, E011, E012, E013, E020, E021, E024, E025, E030, E031). In E001, a pedestrian walks past the wooden crate. In E005-E011, multiple pedestrians are seen walking in the area between the wooden crate, box stacks, and pallet stacks. The large wooden crate and box stacks create significant visual obstructions. In E020 and E021, the close-up view shows how the wooden crate and boxes block the view of the area behind them. In E024 and E025, the box stacks are shown to be tall enough to completely obscure a person standing behind them.
findings.risk_interpretation: Pedestrians can disappear behind the large wooden crate and box stacks, making them invisible to vehicle operators approaching from certain angles. A vehicle operator would not see a pedestrian until they emerge from behind the obstruction, potentially leading to a collision.
findings.applicability_reason: The wooden crate and box stacks obstruct the path of travel and create blind spots where pedestrians and vehicles cannot see each other.
unknowns: Site-specific traffic rules for this area
recommended_actions: Install convex mirrors at key intersection points near the wooden crate and box stacks
Mark pedestrian walkways with clear signage and floor markings
Implement a slow zone with reduced speed limits in this area
Consider relocating the wooden crate and box stacks to improve sight lines
Add spotter or flagger for pedestrian crossings in this area
